blocks.text:
After breakfast, begin a sightseeing tour of the capital.

Quito stands at approximately **2,850 metres** above sea level. Founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca settlement, the city has preserved a vast historic centre despite the earthquake of 1917.

As you walk, discover churches, plazas, colonial façades and old rooftops. The architecture and interiors reflect the Quito School of Art, blending Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous traditions.

Allow approximately **4 hours** to explore the Old Town.

One important stop is the **Church of San Francisco**, associated with the Franciscan order and the development of education and art in Quito.

**Plaza Grande** is home to the Cathedral, the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop’s Palace and other government buildings.

You will also see a Jesuit church with an elaborately decorated façade.

After exploring the historic centre, continue to the equator.

blocks.text:
The first stop is **Ciudad Mitad del Mundo**, a tourist and cultural complex dedicated to the location of the equator.

Here stands the Equatorial Monument, topped by a metal globe representing the Earth.

The complex celebrates Ecuador’s geographical position and the traditional concept of the “Middle of the World”.

blocks.text:
The second stop is the **Intiñán Museum**.

The museum explores Ecuador’s equatorial geography and culture. Interactive experiments demonstrate how ancient peoples identified the position of the equator.

One well-known experiment involves balancing an egg on a nail.

Alongside the demonstrations, the museum displays information about Indigenous peoples, their dwellings, totems and everyday objects.

After the tour, return to Quito.

Check in at **Hotel Finlandia 4★**.

**Meals:** Breakfast.
